question.problem:
Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $5x+2y=75?$

I. $(11,10)$

II. $(10,15)$

III. $(5,25)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's check each pair in turn.

- $(11,10)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=11$ and $y=10,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2y & =75 \\ 5\cdot 11+2\cdot 10 & =75 \\ 55+20 & =75 \\ 75 & =75\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- $(10,15)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=10$ and $y=15,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2y & =75 \\ 5\cdot 10+2\cdot 15 & =75 \\ 50+30 & =75 \\ 80 & \ne 75\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- $(5,25)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=5$ and $y=25,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2y & =75 \\ 5\cdot 5+2\cdot 25 & =75 \\ 25+50 & =75 \\ 75 & =75\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
